Title: 2027 school session to begin Jan 4
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 school session for national and government-aided schools will begin on Jan 4 and end on Dec 2 for Group A states and Dec 3 for Group B states.
The Education Ministry (MoE) said Group A comprises Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu, while Group B covers Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Perak, Perlis, Penang, Sabah, Sarawak, Selangor and the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya.
MoE has also coordinated the festive holidays for the 2027 school session, covering Hari Raya Aidilfitri, Chinese New Year, Hari Raya Aidiladha, Kaamatan, Gawai Dayak, Wesak Day, Deepavali and Christmas.
"All schools must comply with the additional holiday provisions set by MoE in conjunction with Hari Raya Aidilfitri, Chinese New Year, Hari Raya Aidiladha, Wesak Day and Deepavali, with the additional holidays not required to be replaced.
"The ministry has also set Jan 3, 2028 as the start of the 2028 school session for both Group A and Group B states," it said in a statement.
MoE said the standardisation was aimed at ensuring a coordinated opening of the 2028 school session nationwide, while facilitating school administration planning and a more orderly and effective implementation of teaching and learning activities.

Title: 'Heavy plastic bag' turns out to be three mortar bombs
Article:
SEPANG: A lorry driver who picked up a heavy package from a pile of rubbish in Sungai Balak, Kajang, was stunned to discover it contained three mortar bombs.
Making the discovery even more alarming, the Roll On Roll Off (Roro) lorry driver had unknowingly transported the package all the way back to his home in Kampung Dato' Ahmad Razali here.
Md Raduan Ghani, 41, said he had started work as usual around 4am on Friday, collecting and disposing of rubbish.
"I drove the lorry to Sungai Balak in Kajang to carry out rubbish disposal work. I separated some of the heavier items.
"After finishing work, I returned home and the red plastic package which I had separated earlier was still in the lorry. I had no idea what was inside," he said when met outside his home this evening.
Raduan said he began removing the items from the package one by one after arriving home and was shocked when he realised they appeared to be bombs.
He alerted a neighbour, who immediately contacted police.
"I went straight to the Dengkil police station to lodge a report. I never imagined something like this would happen. This is the first time I have ever come across anything like this," he said.
Sepang police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said police received a report from the lorry driver around 3.30pm.
He said personnel from the Dengkil police station secured the area before a Bomb Disposal Unit team from the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) was deployed to the scene.
"An inspection was carried out and the three objects suspected to be bombs were removed to a safe location.
"The situation at the scene is under control and the explosives will be destroyed tomorrow," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: F1 fans complain of gridlocked traffic, over three-hour waits for shuttles
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Formula 1 spectators have complained of gridlocked roads, long shuttle bus queues and poor crowd management at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), after the first day of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia yesterday.
Malaysian X user @tuakdotsol, said this morning that roads heading towards the circuit remained gridlocked, while private cars and e-hailing vehicles were apparently being stopped at the perimeter, funnelling spectators towards shuttle hubs at Mitsui Outlet Park and KLIA Terminal 2.
“Apparently private cars and Grabs are blocked at the perimeter, so everyone funnels into shuttle hubs at Mitsui outlet and KLIA T2,” the user wrote, alongside images showing large crowds near the circuit.
British content creator Ryan Howlett, who is based in Malaysia, said he left Sepang at 5.45pm yesterday but only managed to board a bus at 9pm, describing the experience as “one of the craziest things” he had encountered.
Howlett also alleged that people were fighting, shouting and throwing objects at buses amid the crowds, while criticising what he described as an absence of signs or information when spectators exited the circuit.
Another X user, @saroki19, described the journey from Sepang to KLIA yesterday as “very bad” and “horrendous”, criticising the organisation of the shuttle service and traffic management.
“Really need to think & plan this well. Sunday is going to be hell!” the user wrote, while tagging Rapid KL, the police and KLIA Ekspres.
Malaysian X user @RimauXI also complained yesterday of “super long” bus queues, while noting that access to the circuit from the Sultan Abdul Samad KLIA Mosque roundabout was restricted to authorised vehicles.
The complaints come despite extensive transport arrangements announced ahead of the race, with Rapid KL saying 95 free shuttle buses would run every 10 to 15 minutes from KLIA Terminal 2, Mitsui Outlet Park and Bandar Baru Enstek between 7am and midnight, although frequencies were subject to traffic conditions.
KLIA had warned that more than 200,000 spectators were expected over the three-day event, with daily crowds potentially exceeding 100,000, and advised racegoers to use public transport because of limited parking and expected congestion.
The Bahrain Grand Prix is being held at Sepang from October 2 to 4 after the original Bahrain race could not go ahead, bringing Formula 1 back to the Malaysian circuit for the first time since 2017.

Title: Hannah Yeoh: 8,000 KL businesses renew licences in two months under streamlined system
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 3 — A total of 8,000 businesses in Kuala Lumpur renewed their business licences within two months after a new multi-year renewal initiative was introduced in July.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said 704 businesses opted for a two-year renewal, while 1,802 businesses renewed their licences for three years.
“I am happy to share that in just two months, 8,000 businesses in Kuala Lumpur renewed their licences for one year. For a two-year renewal, they receive a five per cent discount, which 704 businesses have opted for, while 1,802 businesses chose a three-year renewal to enjoy a 10 per cent discount on their business licence,” she said.
She said this at The Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KLSCCCI) 122nd Anniversary Dinner here last night, themed ‘Connecting Businesses, Shaping Tomorrow’.
Hannah said the initiative, which allows businesses to renew licences for up to three years, is part of efforts to ease business transactions with the government, noting that repetitive administrative processes take valuable time away from running a business.
“This may sound like a small change, but if you run a business, these things matter. Every additional process takes time away from running a business.
“If you have complied with the rules, I do not think the government should keep asking you to repeat the same process unnecessarily,” she said.
Meanwhile, KLSCCCI as well as the Associated Chinese Chambers of Commerce and Industry of Malaysia (ACCCIM) president Datuk Ng Yih Pyng welcomed the introduction of business licence renewals for up to three years by Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL).
He said the measure not only reduces repetitive administrative work, but also gives businesses greater certainty to plan ahead.
Ng said the KLSCCCI has remained steadfast in its mission over the past 122 years to unite the business community, represent the voice of businesses, foster commercial and industrial collaboration, and create a more conducive environment for enterprises to grow. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s largest MMEA vessel launched in Türkiye, set to sail home in January
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Construction of the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency’s (MMEA) Multi-Purpose Mission Ship 1 (MPMS 1) is progressing smoothly and ahead of schedule, with the vessel expected to begin its voyage home in late January next year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said that upon completion and handover, MPMS 1 would make history as the largest vessel in the MMEA fleet.
He said the acquisition of the strategic asset would enhance the capabilities of MMEA personnel in carrying out various maritime operations, from enforcement and surveillance of the country’s waters to search and rescue (SAR) operations.
“I am in Istanbul, Türkiye today to witness the launch of MPMS 1, the MMEA’s new vessel being built at Desan Shipyard.
“After going through several stages of planning and construction, we can see that MPMS 1 is now closer to becoming part of MMEA’s assets. Its construction is progressing well and ahead of schedule, which is certainly a positive development,” he said in a post on his official Facebook page yesterday.
Saifuddin Nasution earlier officiated the launch of the vessel at Desan Shipyard in Istanbul, which was witnessed by Türkiye’s Interior Minister Mustafa Ciftci, Türkiye’s Industry and Technology Minister Mehmet Fatih Kacir, Turkish Navy Commander Admiral Ercument Tatlioglu and Desan Shipyard representative Cenk Ismail Kaptanoglu.
Also present were Home Ministry Deputy Secretary-General (Management) Ainah Mohd Soon, MMEA Deputy Director-General (Logistics) Vice Admiral (M) Datuk Saiful Lizan Ibrahim, Malaysian Ambassador to Türkiye Adlan Mohd Shaffieq and Malaysian Consul-General in Istanbul Ahmad Amiri Abu Bakar.
Also present was Economic Ministry Director of the Public Safety and Security Division Wan Ahmad Asmady Wan Md Din.
Meanwhile, the Home Ministry (KDN), in a separate statement, said the launch ceremony, attended by about 200 guests, featured a symbolic bottle-breaking ceremony using seawater from Malaysia.
According to KDN, the ceremony symbolised the close cooperation between the two countries before the vessel was launched into the Sea of Marmara.
In conjunction with the launch, Saifuddin Nasution also held a bilateral meeting with Ciftci to discuss matters of mutual interest, including exploring opportunities for technology-sharing in the security and maritime industries.
“The construction of MPMS 1 is a manifestation of the close ties between Malaysia and the Republic of Türkiye. The acquisition of this strategic asset will strengthen MMEA’s operational capabilities in carrying out its responsibility to safeguard the security and sovereignty of the country’s waters.
“The implementation of this project also opens opportunities to strengthen cooperation in shipbuilding, maritime industry development as well as the sharing of expertise and technology between the two countries,” the ministry said.
KDN said the cooperation reflected Malaysia and Türkiye’s continued commitment to expanding strategic ties that would not only be mutually beneficial but also serve as a catalyst for exploring new areas of cooperation in the future. — Bernama

Title: Husband and wife killed, two daughters seriously injured in Kluang crash
Article:
KLUANG, Oct 3 — A husband and wife were killed, and their two daughters were seriously injured in an accident involving a car and a lorry at Kilometre 72.5 of Jalan Batu Pahat-Mersing this afternoon.
Kluang police chief ACP Bahrin Mohd Noh said the crash involved a lorry driven by a 34-year-old man from Kluang heading towards Kahang and a Hyundai Matrix coming from the opposite direction.
He said investigations found that the Hyundai Matrix, driven by a 54-year-old local man, is believed to have lost control due to slippery road conditions before entering the opposite lane and colliding with the lorry.
“As a result of the collision, the car driver and his 49-year-old wife sustained severe head and bodily injuries and were pronounced dead at the scene.
“The couple’s two daughters, aged 24 and 21, who were in the rear passenger seats, also suffered severe injuries and are currently receiving treatment in the red zone of the Emergency Department at Enche’ Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital, Kluang,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Bahrin said the lorry driver was not injured.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Kluang Fire and Rescue Station commander Jusoh Mohd Salleh said they received an emergency call at 4.53pm. Six firefighters, a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT), and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) unit were sent to the scene.
He said the two victims trapped in the car, identified as Mislan Osman and his wife Nor Azilah A Rahman, were removed using special equipment before being pronounced dead. — Bernama

Title: Motivational speaker under police investigation over alleged child sexual harassment in Perlis
Article:
KANGAR, Oct 3 — Police received a report on September 26 regarding an allegation of sexual harassment of a child by a motivational speaker.
Perlis police chief DCP Hamzah Hashim said the report was lodged at 2.09am and the case is being investigated under Section 12 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
“If convicted, the offender can be jailed up to five years and may also be liable to caning,” he said in a statement yesterday.

Title: Bumper weekend in Malaysia: F1, football legends, concerts and comedy shows set to pack Klang Valley
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — This weekend could feel like a long one for Malaysians in the capital — not because of a string of public holidays, but the sheer number of events expected to clog up roads across the Klang Valley.
The days ahead will feature a flurry of sporting, cultural and musical events, with several taking place simultaneously.
Malay Mail
breaks down some of the biggest events taking place in and around KL this weekend:
Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix

The day jumps will take place between 8.30am and 6pm but the highlight will be the night jumps starting from 8pm to 10pm, which will feature illuminated canopy stunts.
Tokyo Auto Salon Malaysia (Serdang)

Title: How does cloud seeding work? What it could do for haze at Sepang this weekend
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — For more than a month, haze has blanketed parts of Malaysia as transboundary smoke from massive forest and peatland fires in neighbouring Indonesia drifts across the region.
Many of the fires burn deep into carbon-rich peatlands, which are notoriously difficult to extinguish and can produce thick, acrid smoke for prolonged periods.
With the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) set to host the Bahrain F1 Grand Prix this weekend, SIC chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif has said cloud seeding operations could be carried out around the circuit to induce rainfall ahead of the event.
The hope is that the additional rainfall could help improve air quality and visibility, creating better conditions for the race and spectators.
The proposal comes as Malaysia has stepped up cloud seeding operations in response to the haze and hot, dry weather.
Fourteen cloud seeding operations involving more than 50 flights have been carried out nationwide as of September 30, 2026, with operations also extended to Sabah and Sarawak.
National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) operations implementation section director Datuk Mazli Mazlan said the operations were aimed at increasing rainfall, particularly to ensure dam water levels remained sufficient.
So, how exactly does cloud seeding work, what can it achieve, and why is it being considered as one measure to deal with the current conditions?
What is cloud seeding?
Cloud seeding operations are seen over the Air Itam Dam water catchment area in this February 28, 2024 image. — Picture courtesy of PBAPP
Clouds are made up of tiny water droplets or ice crystals that form when water vapour in the atmosphere cools and condenses around microscopic particles such as dust or salt.
These particles, known as condensation nuclei or ice nuclei, provide a surface for water to collect and eventually form larger droplets or ice crystals that can fall as precipitation.
Cloud seeding is a form of weather modification that attempts to enhance this natural process by introducing additional particles into suitable clouds.
It does not create clouds or rain from a clear sky.
Instead, the technique relies on existing clouds that contain sufficient moisture and suitable atmospheric conditions.
How does cloud seeding work?
Preparation of solutions for cloud seeding operations at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) Kuching Air Base in this file picture dated September 20, 2019. — Bernama pic
The process begins with meteorologists identifying suitable clouds — generally those that contain enough moisture but have not yet produced significant rainfall.
Seeding agents are then released into or around the cloud using aircraft, ground-based generators or other methods, depending on the technique being used.
Common seeding materials include silver iodide, which can encourage ice crystal formation in cold clouds, and hygroscopic materials such as salt, which are used in warmer clouds.
Dry ice, or frozen carbon dioxide, can also be used in some cloud seeding operations to cool clouds and encourage ice formation.
Once introduced, the particles provide additional nuclei around which water vapour can condense.
The droplets or ice crystals can then grow as they collect more moisture.
When they become sufficiently large and heavy, they fall from the cloud as precipitation — rain in warm conditions, or snow or hail where temperatures permit.
Cloud seeding therefore works by enhancing precipitation from clouds that are already capable of producing rain, rather than producing rainfall from clear skies.
Three main types of cloud seeding
MetMalaysia personnel prepare a saltwater mixture for cloud seeding before loading the barrels onto an RMAF aircraft at the Subang airbase for operations in Perlis and Kedah on May 11, 2026. — Picture from Facebook/National Disaster Management Agency, Prime Minister’s Department
There are three broad types of cloud seeding, each designed for different cloud and weather conditions:
1. Static seeding
This is one of the most widely used methods. It involves introducing substances such as silver iodide into cold clouds to encourage the formation of ice crystals, which can grow and eventually fall as precipitation.
2. Dynamic seeding
This technique aims to increase the size and vertical development of clouds by altering air movement within them. It requires more material and careful planning, but has the potential to enhance rainfall from suitable clouds.
3. Hygroscopic seeding
Used mainly in warm-cloud environments, this method disperses particles such as salt into clouds. The particles act as nuclei around which water droplets can form and grow, eventually becoming large enough to fall as rain.
What does Malaysia use?
KUCHING, Sept 3 — Malaysian Army (TDM) personnel push tanks containing salt solution into a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) C-130 aircraft to carry out a cloud seeding operation at the RMAF Kuching Base today.
According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), cloud seeding operations in Malaysia use two approaches known as wet seeding and dry seeding.
Both methods rely on hygroscopic materials, such as salt, to encourage the formation and growth of water droplets in suitable clouds.
For wet seeding, a salt solution weighing about 200kg is carried in four tanks aboard a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) C-130 Hercules aircraft.
The solution is sprayed into suitable clouds at an altitude of between 5,000 and 8,000 feet.
For dry seeding, hygroscopic flares mounted on a Cessna 340A aircraft are ignited at the base of suitable clouds at an altitude of between 3,000 and 5,000 feet.
The dispersed salt particles act as Cloud Condensation Nuclei (CCN), providing surfaces around which water vapour can condense and encouraging water droplets to grow until they become sufficiently large and heavy to fall as rain.
Rainfall is typically expected within 30 to 60 minutes after a cloud seeding operation, although the timing depends on prevailing atmospheric conditions and whether the targeted clouds are suitable for seeding.

Title: Rantau Panjang wants its buzz back — and traders hope ECRL is the answer
Article:
PASIR MAS, Oct 2 — Rantau Panjang was once a bustling border town, alive with the pulse of trade; however, the passage of time and a decline in visitor numbers have left some premises quiet, while the remaining traders continue to hope for a turnaround.
The proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) alignment from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is seen not merely as a new transport option, but as a potential catalyst to revitalize economic activities in the town.
For those who have earned their livelihood there for decades, ECRL represents more than just tracks and trains; it offers a chance to see Rantau Panjang return to being a bustling, vibrant hub that draws crowds once again.
A Bernama survey of Rantau Panjang town found that while some businesses are operating as usual, others remain closed reflecting a shift in the business landscape compared to the vibrance locals once experienced.
For the traders who have persevered, customer volume is a key factor in business survival, consequently, any initiative to improve accessibility and the flow of people to the area is eagerly awaited.
Rantau Panjang resident Syed Abu Bakar Syed Daud, 65, who has lived in the area for over 50 years said he has personally witnessed the town's transformation, particularly regarding the number of visitors and traders.
Having started his business more than 44 years ago, he noted that the slump in commercial activity has impacted his own income, forcing him to close two grocery shops and an eatery over the past year.
“When this town was still ‘alive,’ over 1,000 traders operated here, but now fewer than 30 per cent remain, even though visitor numbers are merely modest. In the past, I could make over RM1,000 in daily sales, but before closing my shop, there were times when it was difficult to reach that amount even over two or three days,” he told Bernama recently.
According to Syed Abu Bakar, the shift became more pronounced following the Covid-19 pandemic, as visitor numbers and business activity in the town failed to return to previous levels.
He noted that the proposal to extend the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) to Rantau Panjang offers a glimmer of hope for traders who wish to see the area become a hub of activity once again.
“I was delighted to hear the news that the ECRL is set to be extended to Rantau Panjang. We certainly hope that more people will visit and that the town can come back to life,” he said.
Trader Fu Chee Kat said changing customer patterns have forced him to scale back his business in Rantau Panjang, where he now operates just one shop with one employee. — Bernama pic
For trader Fu Chee Kat, 81, who has been doing business in Rantau Panjang for over 30 years, changing customer patterns have also impacted his operations.
He previously ran two shops selling various goods including kitchenware and bedsheets and employed six workers; however, he was forced to close one shop two years ago and now retains only one employee.
He added that one of the issues raised by customers is their concern regarding taxes on goods purchased in the area.
“There are customers who said they were reluctant to come and shop in this town due to concerns about being charged tax. There are times when they are taxed even after purchasing just a single item. Therefore, I hope the government will look into this matter and re-evaluate it, particularly regarding retail purchases; perhaps the tax could be abolished for retail and applied only to wholesale purchases,” he said.
Fu said if the ECRL extension materialises, the increase in visitor numbers could benefit local traders who still rely on commercial activities in the town.
In this regard, resident Rozila Salleh, 55, expressed deep appreciation of the Madani Government's under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the focus on the development of Rantau Panjang.
She hopes the proposed ECRL extension would drive development and improve transport accessibility in the border area.
“Rantau Panjang is indeed one of the main gateways to Thailand, so extending the ECRL here would provide residents and visitors with another transport option alongside the current land routes.
“We greatly appreciate the Prime Minister and the Madani Government's attention to development in border areas like Rantau Panjang. We hope this initiative becomes a reality, as it would not only benefit residents but also open up broader economic opportunities for local traders,” she said.
Media reports previously indicated that Malaysia and China had agreed to the proposal to extend the ECRL project from Kota Bharu to Rantau Panjang, a move with the potential to establish a direct transport link with Thailand.
Anwar reportedly said the proposal could not only boost the economy of Kelantan’s interior which had previously seen limited development spillover but also strengthen cross-border transport connectivity.
In August, Transport Minister Anthony Loke reportedly said that ECRL Phase 1 (Kota Bharu to Gombak) is targeted to begin operations this December ahead of the original January 2027 schedule subject to the smooth progress of testing and commissioning processes, including System Integration Tests and the Fault-Free Run, without compromising safety. — Bernama

Title: Treat RM220m international maritime trade issue with same urgency as political cases, maritime expert tells MACC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Maritime industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan today questioned why an international maritime trade issue involving petroleum cargo worth more than RM220 million had yet to receive a clear answer from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), when the commission had moved swiftly on cases involving politicians.
Jeyenderan, who is chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, directed his questions at the MACC chief commissioner over a report he lodged on June 5. It concerns alleged discrepancies between the bill of lading and the physical movement of petroleum cargo at Tanjung Langsat, Johor.
“Why is the MACC continuing to remain silent on this issue? Why does it appear that cases involving politicians are being given special attention, while an issue involving international maritime trade has yet to receive a clear answer?” he said in a statement today.
He said that despite several visits to the MACC office and submitting various documents to the authorities, he had yet to receive a final written explanation on the status of the report or any decision made on it.
“I received four emails beginning in June and an SMS in September stating that the case was under ‘MACC Action’, but it has now been four months and there is still no final decision on the report,” he said.
“I have seen several politicians and corporate figures charged in court since May, including former ministers, former senior government officials and company executives, while my report has yet to receive a clear written decision.
“Just tell us whether the case is NFA (No Further Action) or still under investigation. If it is still being investigated, tell us. If it is NFA, tell us. Do not continue to remain silent. We only want to know the status of the report,” he said.
Jeyenderan said he had provided the documents and information requested by the authorities and was not seeking special treatment, only confirmation of whether the matter was still under investigation or had been concluded.
He said the matter should not be viewed as merely a local commercial issue, as it involved international petroleum cargo, trade documentation, Customs procedures, cargo traceability and government revenue.
Jeyenderan also claimed that the Royal Malaysian Customs Department had yet to provide a final written position on the Customs treatment of the cargo, despite repeated requests and discussions with the relevant authorities.
“The MACC is silent and Customs is also silent. We are talking about an international petroleum trade issue involving cargo worth more than RM220 million, yet there is still no proper written explanation on the regulatory position concerning the matter,” said Jeyenderan who has three decades of experience in the industry.
He claimed the absence of a written position had left industry players uncertain on several matters, including the handling of petroleum cargo declared under the K8 procedure, its discharge and storage in shore tanks, and whether mixing or blending it with existing stock was permitted and subject to specific approvals or documentation.
“How can businesses, traders and international players have confidence in the system if the authorities do not provide a clear position on the applicable procedures and requirements?
“We had a meeting with the Ministry of Finance last week. They concluded that no duty was imposed on the cargo as presented. But to date, no authority has provided any explanation in writing,” he said.
Jeyenderan alleged that the prolonged uncertainty could affect not only the parties directly involved but also Malaysia’s reputation as a trade and maritime hub.
He said he respected the investigative and regulatory powers of the MACC and the Customs Department, and understood that certain information might not be disclosed while an investigation was ongoing, but stressed that a clear written position should be provided when legally permissible.
He added that he would continue seeking clarification through the appropriate channels, saying his aim was to obtain certainty on the applicable procedures and documentation requirements, not to secure any particular decision in favour of his company.

Title: Coach Murad seeks clarity on who was behind threats against Caprice after police drop action against him
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — High-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Coach Murad or Murad Zaidi, wants to know who was behind an Instagram account that allegedly posted death threats against social media influencer Caprice and his family, after police decided to take no further action against him.
His lawyer, Aizzat Mustafa, said Murad had initially been investigated in connection with the account, “jefri_yayan”, but was later informed by police that further action against him had been classified as No Further Action (NFA).
However, police confirmed in a written response dated Sept 18 this year that the underlying case remained open and under investigation, he said.
“On July 11 last year, Murad Zaidi was arrested in connection with the investigation. His mobile phone was seized, his residence was searched and several individuals connected to him were also called in to assist in the investigation.
“On Nov 26 last year, police informed Murad Zaidi in writing that the matter against him had been classified as NFA, following which his mobile phone was returned.
“My client has consistently denied being behind the account and cooperated fully with the police investigation,” Aizzat said.
The matter dates back to July 7 last year, when the account allegedly posted comments containing threats, including references to death and bullets, concerning Caprice and members of his family.
Aizzat said the latest position raised two important questions: who was actually behind the account, and why the matter remained unresolved more than a year after the alleged threats were first reported.
“The alleged threats were treated with considerable seriousness and urgency from the outset. Within days, Coach Murad was arrested, his telephone was seized, his residence was searched and persons connected to him were called in for investigation.
“More than a year has now passed. PDRM has confirmed that further action against Coach Murad was classified as NFA, yet the underlying case remains under investigation.
“In those circumstances, my client is entitled to ask what progress has been made in identifying the actual person behind the account and why the investigation has taken this length of time to reach a conclusion,” he said.
Aizzat stressed that Murad was not alleging that police had abandoned the investigation.
“PDRM has expressly confirmed that the matter remains under investigation. What Coach Murad is seeking is clarity on the progress of that investigation and, ultimately, the identity of the person responsible for the account and the alleged threats,” he said.
He said there was also a legitimate question over Caprice’s current position.
“We would like Caprice’s current position to be established, including whether he still maintains that Coach Murad was behind the account and whether he has received any subsequent information from PDRM concerning the identity of the actual operator.
“The allegations had serious consequences for my client and affected his reputation. Now that further action against him has been classified as NFA, he wants the public record to accurately reflect that position,” he said.
Aizzat said Murad had denied being behind the account from the outset and had himself lodged police reports over the matter.
“My client is not seeking confidential information which may prejudice an ongoing investigation.
“He simply wants an investigation which began with considerable urgency more than a year ago to reach a proper conclusion, and for the actual person responsible for the alleged threats to be identified.
“If Coach Murad was not the person against whom further action was ultimately taken, the obvious question remains: who was actually behind ‘jefri_yayan’?” he said.
Aizzat added that Murad hoped the investigation would be concluded without further delay so the matter could finally be clarified for all parties concerned.

Title: PM Anwar hails three more golds as Malaysia matches best-ever Asian Games haul
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated Malaysian athletes on winning three more gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games in Japan today, describing the achievement as a proud accomplishment that reflected their outstanding ability and determination.
He said the latest haul brought Malaysia’s gold medal tally to nine as the national contingent continued its campaign to make the Jalur Gemilang proud on the Asian stage, matching Malaysia’s best-ever gold medal haul at the Asian Games, won at the 2010 Guangzhou edition.
“Congratulations and well done to today’s gold medallists,” he said in a Facebook post today.
The three gold medals were won by national track cycling ace Datuk Mohd Azizulhasni Awang in the men’s keirin at the Izu Velodrome, while Malaysia also dominated the women’s and men’s team squash events at the Nagoya Kinjo Futo Arena.
In the women’s final, the team comprising Aifa Azman, S. Sivasangari, Aira Azman and Rachel Arnold defeated Hong Kong 2-1, while the men’s squad of Ng Eain Yow, Sanjay Jeeva, C. Ameeshenraj and Mohammad Syafiq Kamal beat Pakistan 2-0.
Anwar also urged Malaysians to continue praying for the success of the national athletes competing in tomorrow’s finals.
“Tomorrow, the battle for gold continues with the men’s padel pairing of Christian Didier Chin and Aidan Yunus, as well as the men’s hockey squad, who will compete in their respective finals. Let us all pray for their success,” he said. — Bernama

Title: No power struggles, says Selangor Sultan as current and former menteris besar meet
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 2 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today met and dined with two former Selangor menteris besar, Mohamad Khir Toyo and Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, as well as the current Menteri Besar, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The special meeting took place after the recitation of
Yasin
,
tahlil
and prayers for safety held in conjunction with the Silver Jubilee celebration of His Royal Highness’ 25-year reign at the Sultan Salahuddin Abdul Aziz Shah Mosque, here.
“This meeting reflects the Sultan of Selangor’s continuous concern regarding the state’s direction and the people’s livelihood, whilst demonstrating the good relationship between the royal institution and the state’s administrative leadership, including those who previously shouldered the responsibility,” according to a post on the Selangor Royal Office Facebook page.
According to the post, Sultan Sharafuddin advised political leaders not to fight, squabble or wrestle for power to the point of triggering division among themselves.
Instead, he wanted all efforts and attention to be focused on the state’s development, the well-being of the people, and the welfare of those in need.
His Royal Highness also said that differences in stance and political ideologies should not be a barrier to cooperation for the benefit of the state and its people.
“Leadership responsibilities must be carried out with full trustworthiness, prioritising the people’s interests above personal or political group interests.
“His Royal Highness also reminded that Selangor’s progress must be accompanied by societal harmony and administrative stability.
“Hence, leaders must maintain an attitude of mutual respect and prioritise constructive discussions in addressing any differences,” the post stated. — Bernama

Title: Man detained after 230kg of subsidised cooking oil found hidden among rubbish at Melaka restaurant
Article:
MELAKA, Oct 2 — A Yemeni man in his 50s has been detained today for investigation into suspected unlawful possession of subsidised cooking oil at an Arab food restaurant in Bukit Baru here.
Melaka Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director Dr Mohd Hazimin Jamaludin said 230 kilogrammes of packaged cooking oil worth RM575 were found during an Op Tiris 4.0 raid at the premises at about 1.30pm today.
He said the restaurant, which has been operating since 2014, was suspected of misappropriating subsidised cooking oil for commercial purposes following a public complaint and three weeks of intelligence gathering.
The subsidised cooking oil, comprising various brands, was found in several black plastic bags placed among a pile of dry waste, including old carpets, in a corner of the third floor of the premises, which had been converted into a workers’ dormitory.
“The packaged cooking oil was found in several black plastic bags placed among a pile of dry waste such as old carpets in a corner of the third floor of the premises, which had been converted into a workers’ dormitory,” he said in a statement here today.
Mohd Hazimin said the staircase leading to the third floor had been modified to avoid detection by the authorities, and the controlled goods were found during an inspection that lasted about 30 minutes.
He said preliminary investigations found that the packaged cooking oil was delivered together with other dry goods using a courier service, while the orders were allegedly placed by the restaurant’s headquarters in Kuala Lumpur.
Mohd Hazimin said the Yemeni man, who was the restaurant supervisor, was detained to assist investigations under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961 for possessing controlled goods under circumstances giving rise to reasonable suspicion of an offence.
He said an individual convicted of the offence could be fined up to RM1 million or imprisoned for up to three years, or both, while a company could be fined up to RM2 million for a first offence.
Meanwhile, he reminded individuals and companies not to manipulate, misappropriate or deal in controlled goods without valid permits and licences. — Bernama

Title: Penang Free School marks 210 years with push for digital transformation
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 2 — Penang Free School (PFS), the oldest English-medium school in South-east Asia, is marking its 210th anniversary this year and is committed to strengthening its digital capabilities to better prepare students for the changing education and technology landscape.
PFS Organising Committee chairman Ivan Ooi Jieun Vei said the anniversary celebrations also provided an opportunity to mobilise support for the PFS Digital Transformation Fund, aimed at enhancing the school’s digital infrastructure and capabilities.
“This is not merely a celebration of 210 years of history. It is a rallying call to the entire Penang Free School community to step forward together and invest in the school’s future.
“We want to harness the strengths of our alumni, educators, industry and the community to ensure that students not only excel academically but are also capable of developing into future professionals, innovators and leaders,” he said.
He said the fund focused on strengthening digital infrastructure, enhancing educators’ capabilities and exposing students to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, coding and new digital technologies.
Ooi said that as of September 28, a total of 13 75-inch Hisense Smartboards had been acquired through the PFS Digital Transformation Initiative, out of an overall target of 33 units to be installed throughout the school.
He added that the Digital Transformation Fund aimed to complement, rather than replace, government funding to accelerate the school’s development.
“We are not raising funds merely to acquire technology. We are investing in capabilities, opportunities and ultimately, in the talent development that will underpin Penang’s future economy,” he said.
The highlight of the celebration is the 210th Anniversary Dinner at PFS tomorrow from 6pm to 11.30pm, featuring a special performance by Malaysia’s Queen of Rock, Ella, alongside performances by PFS students. — Bernama

Title: HKL emergency dept upgrade enters final phase, completion targeted by end-2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The upgrading project of the new block of the Emergency and Trauma Department at the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) is now in the final phase of implementation.
The HKL Management said today that several issues require repair and improvement work in the inspection and completion process before the facility can be fully completed.
“The related work is being given attention and priority, with a resolution expected to be implemented by the end of 2026,” said the statement.
HKL said that it is committed to ensuring that all repair work is carried out properly to meet the facility’s safety, functional, and quality requirements before the project is finalised.
The operation and delivery of health services at the HKL Emergency and Trauma Department will continue as usual during this period.
HKL also appreciates the public’s cooperation, patience, and understanding throughout the upgrading works and apologises for any difficulties that may arise. — Bernama

Title: KL woman fined RM24,000 over fraudulent transfer of retiree’s RM1.1m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — An unemployed woman was fined RM24,000 by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of fraudulently transferring RM1.1 million belonging to a retiree into her own bank account eight years ago.
Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad imposed the fine on Chin Chew Woon, 43, and ordered her to serve 24 months’ imprisonment if she failed to settle the fine.
According to the charges, Chin was accused of transferring RM500,000 and RM600,000 belonging to a 66-year-old man into her bank account in Brickfields on December 26 and 27, 2018.
She was charged under Section 424 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum penalty of five years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both.
According to the facts of the case, the victim received a call from an individual who introduced himself as a police officer, claiming the victim was involved in a money laundering case.
The victim was then instructed to transfer his savings amounting to RM500,000 and RM600,000 into the accused’s account for investigation purposes.
Subsequently, the victim was unable to contact the individual claiming to be a police officer to recover the money.
Investigations revealed that the accused was the owner of the account that received the RM1.1 million. She failed to provide a satisfactory explanation regarding the transactions.
Deputy public prosecutor Anis Hakimah Ibrahim urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence, taking into account the substantial losses suffered by the victim and the prevalence of such fraudulent cases in Malaysia.
Chin, who was unrepresented, pleaded for a lenient sentence on the grounds that she is unemployed and has to support two children, her mother and her ailing mother-in-law. — Bernama

Title: JPJ suspends all MYEG Group services from Oct 5 over unresolved contractual obligations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will suspend all of its services offered through the MYEG Group from October 5, citing contractual obligations that remain unfulfilled or unresolved.
In a statement today, JPJ said the suspension covers My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Berhad, which act as collection agents on behalf of the department, and will take effect at 12.01am on Sunday.
“The decision was made after taking into account compliance with the terms and conditions stipulated in the agreement, as well as obligations that have yet to be fulfilled or resolved by the companies concerned,” JPJ said.
As a result, all JPJ services currently available through MYEG Group channels will be suspended from October 5.
The department said motorists would still be able to carry out transactions through official and alternative channels, including JPJ counters, the MyJPJ app, its public portal, kiosks, Mobile JPJ units and post offices, depending on the type of transaction.
These include renewals of motor vehicle licences, commonly known as road tax, and driving licences, as well as applications for learner driving licences and the checking and payment of traffic summonses.
Vehicle ownership transfers can meanwhile be carried out through JPJ counters, selected kiosks, the JPJ public portal and eAuto for certain transactions.
JPJ said bookings for the Computerised Highway Code Test, or KPP01, made through MYEG before October 5 would remain valid and could proceed as scheduled.
New bookings from October 5 must instead be made through KPP test centres at driving institutes nationwide.
For non-Malaysians paying traffic summonses at the Malaysia-Singapore border, Mobile JPJ units will be available at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex and Bangunan Sultan Iskandar in Johor from 8am to 10pm.
MYEG has for years provided online access to a range of government-related transactions, including JPJ services such as road tax and driving licence renewals.
The latest move also comes as more JPJ transactions are available directly through the department’s own digital channels, including the MyJPJ app and public portal.
JPJ urged the public to use the official channels provided to ensure transactions could be carried out smoothly and securely, adding that it remained committed to ensuring continuity in service delivery.

Title: RM5,000 trial payout leads Pontian victim into RM1.15m investment scam
Article:
PONTIAN, Oct 2 — A private-sector employee lost RM1.15 million after falling victim to an online investment scam operated by a syndicate.
Pontian District Police Chief Supt Hadzrat Hussein Mion Hussain said police received a report from the 52-year-old man yesterday, with preliminary investigations finding that the incident began in early January after he got acquainted with a woman via WhatsApp.
He said the woman, who introduced herself as ‘Farini’, offered an investment scheme purportedly capable of providing returns of up to 15 per cent of the capital invested.
“The victim made an initial transaction of RM5,000 on February 8 to a bank account provided as a trial and subsequently received RM5,877.65, which was said to be the investment return.
“Convinced by the investment, the victim subsequently made several more transactions to several bank accounts in stages until March 26, 2026, involving a total of RM1,151,621.96,” he said in a statement today.
Hadzrat Hussein said the victim only realised he had been duped after being asked to make an additional payment to enable him to withdraw the investment profits.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Johor conservation efforts produce about 5,000 turtle hatchlings a year
Article:
MERSING, Oct 2 — Johor continues to make positive progress in turtle conservation, particularly for hawksbill and green turtles, with an estimated 5,000 hatchlings emerging each year through protection efforts at nesting sites and hatcheries.
Johor Department of Fisheries director Rosmawati Ghazali said the main turtle nesting sites identified include Pulau Apil, Pulau Dayang, Pulau Besar and Pulau Tinggi here.
She said Pulau Tinggi recorded the highest number of hatchings due to its low population and remote location, which helps minimise human disturbance and threats from predators such as dogs and monitor lizards.
However, Rosmawati said turtle eggs left to hatch naturally face a high risk of predation, so they transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries for closer monitoring.
“When turtles lay their eggs in natural nests, they face many predators and the survival rate is low. Therefore, we transfer eggs found at nesting sites to hatcheries so our personnel can monitor them more closely,” she said.
She spoke to Bernama after inspecting the deployment of cheese block artificial reefs for coral restoration modules in the waters off Pulau Tinggi here recently.
Rosmawati said the Fisheries Conservation and Protection Branch’s conservation efforts are important, as studies show that only one in every 1,000 turtle hatchlings released into the sea is expected to reach maturity.
She said the department is continuing to step up conservation programmes, including education and awareness initiatives with students and local communities, as well as deploying artificial reefs to help preserve the marine ecosystem.
According to Rosmawati, turtle hatchlings face predators on land, in the sea and from the air after hatching, while also needing to find suitable feeding grounds to survive and grow.
She said temperature also plays an important role in determining the sex of turtle hatchlings, with warmer temperatures tending to produce more females and cooler temperatures more males.
“Sometimes we find unfertilised eggs, so we need to ensure the temperature in the area is suitable to produce male hatchlings, as one female needs four males for fertilisation.
“Therefore, we have set a ratio of five males to 10 females here,” she said, adding that the site is monitored regularly, with information recorded through the Fisheries Resources Management System, MyFiRSt.
Rosmawati said there is also a hatchery on Pulau Besar, but the island records relatively few turtle landings and faces constraints in electricity and water supply.
However, she said the department would transfer turtle eggs found on Pulau Besar to the Pulau Tinggi hatchery, which has better facilities for closer monitoring.
She said controlling human activity in hatchery areas is also important as they are sensitive locations where public access is discouraged. — Bernama

Title: JB-Singapore RTS Link service start pushed back to February 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Passenger service on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is now expected to begin in February 2027, the Malaysian and Singaporean governments said today.
In a joint statement, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Singapore Grantor) and the Ministry of Transport Malaysia (Malaysia Grantor) said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline.
The service was previously expected to commence in January. The new target is subject to RTSO obtaining independent safety certification for the RTS Link and securing final regulatory approvals.
The grantors said infrastructure works in both countries are substantially complete and on track to support passenger service once the remaining testing and commissioning activities are satisfactorily completed.
“More time is needed for the remaining activities prior to service commencement,” the statement said.
RTSO expects to complete its final system tests and trial runs by Dec 31, 2026. It will then need safety certification from an independent safety assessor.
Authorities from both countries must review the certification and be satisfied with it before they grant approval to begin passenger operations.
The grantors said they will continue working with RTSO to facilitate the “smooth and safe” delivery of the project.

Title: MCMC, MACC to use AI in fight against corruption and abuse of power
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will leverage artificial intelligence (AI) technology to detect, prevent and manage the risks of abuse of power and misappropriation more systematically and effectively.
In a statement today, MCMC said this was among the areas of collaboration agreed upon by the two agencies through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen strategic cooperation in enforcement, corruption prevention and integrity empowerment in addressing complex challenges in the digital environment.
The exchange of the MoU between MCMC chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din and MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman took place at the MCMC headquarters here today.
The MoU outlines a more coordinated cross-agency approach through the sharing of expertise in enforcement, investigation, digital technology, information management and corruption prevention, including best practices in governance, integrity and risk management.
“Both agencies will also expand collaboration in knowledge and skills development through advocacy programmes, training, knowledge sharing and capacity building, while leveraging technology, including AI.
“Related initiatives can be extended to the industry and relevant stakeholders,” it said.
The MCMC said the effort was expected to enhance the preparedness of both agencies in tackling increasingly complex corruption and misconduct risks, while supporting accountability and effective public service delivery.
“In line with its role as the driver of the nation’s communications and multimedia ecosystem, the MCMC will continue to play a facilitating role in expanding inter-agency synergy towards a more transparent, ethical and responsible work culture.
“This will concurrently boost the confidence of the people, industry and investors in public institutions and the nation’s communications and multimedia ecosystem,” it added. — Bernama

Title: Anwar secures fast-track process for missing Malaysians in Nepal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah has assured Malaysia of full cooperation to determine the status of 54 citizens still missing after devastating floods and landslides in Nepal, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
The update came after one of 55 Malaysians previously listed as missing was located safe and made contact with the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu, according to family representatives and official updates.
“I have had conversations with the prime minister. He is willing to give all the cooperation,” Anwar said to reporters this afternoon, adding that Shah agreed during a bilateral call to facilitate administrative and legal efforts to help relatives obtain closure as quickly as possible.
“We have asked the attorney-general to follow through.”
The standard legal procedures in Nepal typically require a three-year waiting period to issue a death certificate for missing persons, compared to six or seven years under Malaysian law, Anwar said.
However, Nepalese authorities have agreed to support expedited court applications.
“He assured me that he will give all the cooperation necessary to facilitate so that the families can get the results as soon as possible,” Anwar added.
Dr Manivannan Rethinam, a spokesman for Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH), a group representing the victims’ relatives, confirmed that the Foreign Ministry had officially notified them of the located citizen, who has since returned to Malaysia.
Families of 55 Malaysians still missing in Nepal had sought Anwar’s help to intervene in securing an expedited declaration of death, worried they cannot afford to remain in legal and financial limbo for the seven-year period under existing procedures.

Title: Department mobilises 153 firefighters, medevac teams and buses to ensure optimum safety during F1
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A total of 155 officers and members, along with 12 assets from the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), have been deployed to ensure that the levels of safety, emergency preparedness, and rescue operations are at an optimum level throughout the hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026, scheduled to take place at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the assignment is part of the department’s commitment to supporting the organisation of international-level sports events in Malaysia, and this is in addition to ensuring safety and operational readiness aspects are always at the best level.
The department is always ready to provide support in organising large-scale events, especially those involving the public as well as participants and delegates from both within and outside the country.
“The assignment of JBPM officers, personnel, and assets to strategic locations is to ensure that any emergency and rescue needs can be addressed quickly, orderly and effectively,” he said in a statement today.
He said that 12 departmental assets are being mobilised throughout the event, comprising a Fire Rescue Tender, two Compact Fire Rescue Tenders, one 10,000-litre water tanker, three Emergency Medical Rescue Services ambulances and four JBPM buses.
According to him, an A109E helicopter has also been stationed at the SIC to strengthen JBPM’s operational readiness and to support monitoring, emergency and rescue operations if needed.
Regarding personnel, Nor Hisham said that 153 officers and firefighters, comprising fire marshals, medical teams, and medevac personnel, have been assigned to the location for preparedness purposes.
He also said that coordination involving the JBPM, organisers, and related agencies has also been strengthened to ensure that the operational readiness level throughout the grand prix remains at the designated level.
“The safety of visitors, participants, officers, and all parties involved is a priority, and JBPM will ensure that every assignment is carried out based on the established standard operating procedures,” he added.
The organisation of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix 2026 over three days, starting today, is a world-class motorsport event that has returned to Malaysia after Sepang last hosted a Formula 1 race in 2017. — Bernama

Title: Police arrest 13 in Teluk Intan raids, syndicate used Alipay accounts to move gambling proceeds
Article:
TELUK INTAN, Oct 2 — Police have arrested 13 people over a syndicate that allegedly used Alipay accounts opened with Malaysians’ passport details to receive and transfer proceeds from online gambling scams targeting Chinese nationals.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the suspects, comprising five Malaysians and eight Myanmar nationals aged between 20 and 44, were arrested in two raids here on Sept 28.
They were believed to have acted as the syndicate’s leaders and agents responsible for processing the accounts.
“Investigations found that the syndicate acted as a payment gateway agent to transfer proceeds from online gambling scams targeting Chinese nationals.
“The modus operandi involved using mobile phones for facial scans and offering RM500 to locals willing to open Alipay accounts by providing their Malaysian passport details,” he told a press conference at the Hilir Perak district police headquarters today.
Mohd Alwi said the syndicate, believed to have been operating since mid-July, had opened about 60 Alipay accounts using the personal details of local residents.
It allegedly earned a two per cent commission on each transaction, generating an estimated RM2,000 a day.
Police seized 65 mobile phones, a laptop, eight Malaysian passports, 71 SIM cards and an SUV worth RM190,000 during the raids. The case is being investigated under Sections 424A and 120(b).
On another development, Mohd Alwi said police have not ruled out secret society involvement in the shooting of a 41-year-old businessman at a petrol station in Bidor on Sept 29.
“We are not ruling out that possibility, but a thorough investigation will be conducted before any conclusion is reached,” he said, adding that police have recorded statements from 10 witnesses, including the victim.
The businessman suffered a gunshot wound to his left shoulder after he was allegedly shot by two armed assailants at a petrol station in Bidor Sentral at about 6 pm.
He is in stable condition after undergoing surgery at Seri Manjung Hospital. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal overturns acquittal, jails ex‑bowling coach two more years for molesting 13‑year‑old
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — A former bowling coach, already serving a prison term for sexual assault, was sentenced to an additional two years’ imprisonment by the Court of Appeal today for molesting another former Malaysia Games male athlete in 2017.
A three-member bench led by Federal Court judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin, sitting as a Court of Appeal judge, ordered Mat Salleh Jalani to begin serving the two-year sentence after completing his six-year prison term for sexually assaulting a 14-year-old male athlete in 2018.
The bench, which also comprised Justices Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, allowed the prosecution’s appeal to set aside the High Court’s decision to acquit and discharge Mat Salleh of the charge.
The court reinstated the Magistrates’ Court’s conviction and increased the sentence from 18 months to two years’ imprisonment.
In delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Hayatul Akmal said the High Court judge erred in assessing the available evidence and misdirected himself in finding SP3’s (the third prosecution witness and the victim) testimony unconvincing.
He held that the victim’s credibility remained intact and that the court had carefully assessed their testimony.
He further found that the victim’s evidence could stand on its own and was corroborated by other witnesses.
“Delay in lodging a police report regarding a sexual offence does not, in itself, undermine the victim’s credibility,” said Justice Hayatul Akmal, citing a Federal Court decision which recognised that victims may be reluctant to report such incidents for various reasons.
Mat Salleh, 63, was convicted by the Magistrates’ Court on Jan 31, 2024, of outraging the modesty of the victim, who was then 13 years old.
The offence was committed in Kuala Terengganu, Terengganu, at 5pm in May 2017. He was sentenced to 18 months’ imprisonment.
On Aug 22 of the same year, the High Court acquitted and discharged him of the charge, prompting the prosecution to appeal.
At today’s proceedings, Deputy Public Prosecutor Ahmad Nazneen Zulkifli urged the court to increase the sentence, submitting that this was not Mat Salleh’s first offence and that he was currently serving a prison sentence in another case.
Defence lawyer Muhammad Faris Mohamad Fauzi had earlier requested that the court retain the prison sentence imposed by the Magistrates’ Court.
On March 11 this year, the Court of Appeal upheld Mat Salleh’s six-year imprisonment sentence for sexually assaulting a 14-year-old male athlete in 2018. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms expected in KL, Selangor and nine states until 7pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for multiple states across Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah, forecasting heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 7pm today.
In the weather advisory issued at 4pm, MetMalaysia indicated that the adverse weather will affect the entire northern states of Perlis, Kedah, Penang, and Perak, alongside the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
In Selangor, seven districts are on alert: Petaling, Sepang, Kuala Selangor, Sabak Bernam, Klang, Kuala Langat, and Gombak.
In Negeri Sembilan, the warning applies to Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, and Tampin, while in Melaka, it covers Jasin and Alor Gajah. Further south in Johor, affected districts include Mersing, Tangkak, Muar, and Batu Pahat.
On the East Coast, stormy weather is forecast across Machang and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan; Besut, Setiu, and Hulu Terengganu in Terengganu; alongside Jerantut, Pekan, and Rompin in Pahang.
Sarawak and Sabah
In Sarawak, the advisory covers several central and northern divisions, including Sarikei (Maradong and Sarikei), Mukah (Tanjung Manis, Daro, and Mukah), Sibu (Selangau), Kuching, Kapit (Kapit and Belaga), and Limbang.
In Sabah, the warning spans multiple districts across five administrative divisions, encompassing Ranau and Kota Belud on the West Coast, as well as Tambunan, Sook, Keningau, Sipitang, Tenom, and Pensiangan in the Interior.
The alert also extends to the Tawau division (Tawau, Kunak, Lahad Datu, and Kalabakan), the Sandakan division (Kinabatangan, Paitan, Sandakan, Labuk and Sugut, and Telupid), and the Kudat division (Kota Marudu and Pitas).
MetMalaysia explained that a thunderstorm warning is triggered when cloud formations indicate imminent heavy rainfall with an intensity exceeding 20mm per hour, or when precipitation is expected to last for more than an hour.
The department emphasised that these alerts serve as short-term warnings and remain valid for a maximum duration of six hours from the time of issuance.

Title: Ahmad Maslan urges BN to announce Melaka candidates early, give time to meet voters
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Oct 2 — Umno Supreme Council member Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan has suggested that Barisan Nasional (BN) announce its candidate list for the Melaka state election early.
Ahmad, who is also Umno War Room Secretariat chief, said an early announcement would give shortlisted candidates sufficient time to prepare and introduce themselves to voters.
“The earlier, the better. We hope the best candidates will be fielded, whether they are incumbents or new faces,” he told reporters after attending the handover ceremony of completed Public Works Department (JKR) projects to the Education Ministry at SMK Durian Tunggal here today.
Ahmad, who is also Deputy Public Works Minister, said BN’s candidates for the Melaka state election would undergo three levels of screening before a final decision is made by the party’s top leadership. — Bernama

Title: KL Marathon goes ahead this weekend, but Kids Dash cancelled over haze concerns
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – The Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 will proceed this weekend despite the haze, but organisers have cancelled the Kids Dash races to protect the health of young participants.
In a race update, organisers said the Full Marathon, ASICS Half Marathon, IHH 10km and 5km will run as scheduled. The decision followed discussions with the relevant parties and had the support of co-organiser Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur and title sponsor Standard Chartered Malaysia.
“We regret to announce that the Kids Dash races will be cancelled, in the best interest of the children,” the organisers said.
“We are disappointed but we have to prioritise the health and safety of the children over letting them run in less than perfect conditions.”
Parents of Kids Dash participants may collect their child’s race entitlement by presenting the race bib at the Information Counter at Dataran Merdeka tomorrow, from 8am to 12pm.
Organisers also urged adult runners to take their own health into account.
“You know your body best. If you have underlying health issues, please weigh your options carefully before deciding to run,” they said.
They added that conditions will be monitored throughout Saturday and expressed hope for favourable weather on Sunday.
Government expected events to proceed
The announcement follows comments earlier this week by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who said on Sept 30 that the government expected the marathon, the Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, which Malaysia is hosting this weekend, and Le Tour de Langkawi to proceed despite haze affecting parts of the country.
Speaking at a press conference in Putrajaya, Fahmi said the haze was being monitored daily and that the Youth and Sports Ministry would make decisions on the events based on prevailing conditions.
The haze has pushed air quality into the unhealthy range in several parts of the country, raising concerns for athletes, spectators and event personnel taking part in prolonged outdoor activities.

Title: State governments urged to gazette paddy land as rice self‑sufficiency drops to 54.3pc
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — State governments have been urged to gazette paddy-growing areas to sustain rice cultivation and strengthen the country’s food security after the rice self-sufficiency ratio (SSR) declined last year.
SSR measures how much of a country’s domestic demand for a particular food or agricultural product it can meet with its own production.
According to the Agriculture and Food Security Ministry (KPKM), the proposal was among the matters discussed at the second 2026 Agriculture and Food Security Ministers’ Meeting with state agriculture executive councillors, chaired by Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu yesterday.
KPKM said the proposal takes into account the decline in rice cultivation areas, which contributed to the fall in the rice SSR from 68 per cent in 2018 to 54.3 per cent in 2025, as well as a recommendation in the Auditor-General’s Report to gazette padi-growing areas to preserve the amount of land used for rice cultivation.
“Malaysia’s reliance on imported rice was estimated at 1.416 million metric tonnes, worth RM2.953 billion, in 2025,” KPKM said in a statement today.
Agriculture executive councillors from nine states, representatives from the state Economic Planning Units, the Finance Ministry and the Economy Ministry, as well as senior officers, department heads and agency chiefs under KPKM attended the meeting.
KPKM said the meeting also discussed measures to strengthen the country’s food-producing areas by zoning them in structure and local plans, in line with the National Land Use Master Plan.
Among the measures are the immediate gazetting of 24 state agro-food areas under the Permanent Food Production Parks, Permanent Ruminant Production Parks and Aquaculture Industry Zones, as well as implementing the Livestock Farm Regularisation Scheme and Food Area Protection Mechanism in Sabah and Sarawak.
“These measures support KPKM’s efforts to raise the SSR for strategic commodities while increasing domestic production and strengthening the country’s food resilience and security,” the statement said.
KPKM said the meeting also considered a proposal for state governments to participate in Malaysia Fest in Singapore, which has served as a platform to promote Malaysian agro-food products since 2006 through the Malaysia Fruits, Food Fiesta programme, giving local entrepreneurs greater opportunities to enter the Singapore market.
“Malaysia Fest has shown positive growth, with attendance rising from 75,000 in 2017 to 179,400 in 2025, while sales increased from RM6.59 million to RM15.8 million,” it said.
According to the ministry, the meeting also reviewed the status of the National Agro-Food Empowerment Programme under the 13th Malaysia Plan, with 347 projects worth RM349.15 million approved out of 782 applications totalling RM2.09 billion received this year.
Also discussed were the findings of the 2024 Outcome Evaluation Study of the Land Optimisation Programme with state governments, involving 97 projects, 19,447 participants, about 40,000 hectares and RM149.59 million in funding, to assess the programme’s effectiveness and benefits to target groups and the agro-food sector.
On industry regulation, the meeting acknowledged the drafting of the Fertiliser Bill to establish a more structured, transparent and effective regulatory framework for the fertiliser industry, particularly on quality, distribution and price stability, as well as protecting farmers’ interests. — Bernama

Title: MCMC probes AI‑manipulated footage of Dr Mahathir grieving wife’s death, warns of legal action
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 2 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has its eyes on social media content that allegedly uses artificial intelligence (AI) to manipulate footage of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad grieving the death of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali.
The commission said it had contacted the relevant social media platforms over the content.
“If there were any violation of the law, appropriate action may be taken under existing legislation, including the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588),” it said in a statement today.
MCMC said manipulating genuine footage in ways that could mislead the public, distort the context of an event or undermine the dignity of individuals and their families should not be taken lightly, particularly during bereavement.
It urged the public not to create or share misleading manipulated content and to verify material before sharing it.
Suspected manipulated content should also be reported to the relevant platforms or authorities.
While AI offered significant benefits, MCMC stressed that the technology must be used responsibly.
“Technology should not be used to distort the truth or exploit someone’s grief at the expense of dignity and humanity,” it said.
The statement followed the circulation of manipulated footage of Tun Dr Mahathir after his wife’s death on Sept 28 at the age of 100.
In March, the government said AI and deepfake technology was increasingly being used to produce false or manipulated content, including material featuring the images and voices of public figures.
It said MCMC was working with social media platforms and enforcement agencies to address harmful online content. — Bernama
